_about: Cook with Nani proof of concept (24 Sept 2026). Every Kutchi string here is a DRAFT. Words marked source 'zafar-24sep' were confirmed by Zafar as right for now (khun, not khand). Sentences only recombine frames already in the content master (Muke {x} khape / Ne {x} / Salamun alaykum / Wa alaikum salaam / Aabhar aanjo / Achija / Arre re / Hedo / Ghan). Cooking verbs have NO Kutchi yet: they are shown as gestures, and listed in docs/archive/language/cook-with-nani-words.md for the family. Phase A (24 Sept 2026): words with kutchi null are ENGLISH PLACEHOLDERS shown in grey italic until the family supplies the Kutchi (see docs/language/mum-questions/Questions for Mum (Round 2 — Cooking).md). 25 Sept 2026: seven more words (ph-no, ph-slowly, ph-quickly, ph-half, ph-full, ph-big, ph-small) came from Zafar written phonetically over chat, temporary and unconfirmed (Mum to confirm). Each has `kutchi` (a readable romanised spelling, shown on screen) and `say` (Zafar's own phonetic spelling, used for the voice only, never shown). 26 Sept 2026: Mum's A8 and Section B answers (docs/language/grammar-notes.md §23-§28) replaced most English placeholders and Zafar's phonetic drafts; every change is listed in docs/archive/language/cook-word-changes-B.md.
_words: The item catalogue (step 4d): each thing's picture (image), drawn heap, bowl, piece and layer, and joinless, by Cook's id. Its words (Kutchi, English, gender, forms, voice spelling) are the language engine's (data/lang/; their old home is data/lang/seed/cook.json); Cook's ids are the engine's aliases.

meanings._about: Step 4d (decision 42): which language-engine meaning each of Cook's frame keys asks for (data/lang/abstract.json; the same map as build/lang/hand/cook-map.mjs FRAMES). "$x" is the thing the game fills in. The engine builds the words, their agreement and the clip plan (js/cook/words.js); a frame the engine has no rule for comes back as its gap (grey-italic English, flagged to record). Fixed lines need no row here: the engine knows them by the alias cook.line.<key>. Cook's lines, grammar and words moved to the engine's own source, data/lang/seed/cook.json (build/lang/import_cook.mjs reads them there). A fixed line said as a call (Salamun alaykum!, Shabash!) names its Exclaim / Ask here, as Cook says it; the engine knows the words by the alias.

verdicts._about: Words shown over the action after a timing or a pour (English UI). Mechanics name them by key.

pantry._about: Wave 6 (docs/design-language/ux-principles.md 7): Nani's list from the pantry, the smallest round and the first thing a new player does. She says the first thing with Muke {x} de (give me), then Ne {x} for the rest, in any order; you tap each into the basket. Level 1 = three things from the kitchen basics, each level one more (and a fuller shelf: mechanics.fetch.levels). free: false keeps it out of customers' orders.
pantry.name: ph-pantry

forDish._about: 29 Sept (Q6, Zafar): in story mode the first time each of these dishes is made that day starts with a pantry trip for its things (a second one that day doesn't; free play and the lab skip it). What each dish's trip fetches, all stocked in the pantry (shelf art), in the order Nani asks

pantry.how: Listen to what Nani needs, then tap each one into the basket.

headline._was: headline-pantry / -plain (Bring me these for {dish}); T1: Muke de

say._frame: PAN-02 (step 4d): every thing Nani asks for is its own full sentence (Muke atto de.), never the verbless Ne atto.; one sentence with a list waits for Mum's list rule (gap list: Fetch, L29)

chai.name: cook-chai
chai._about: The Chai tray (js/cook/stations/chai-tray.js): a cup for each person on the tray, each with their face. The customer orders chai at the counter; at the tray each person says how they like theirs (dudh or dudh na; Muke chai me {n} khun khape or khun na; plain, elchi waari chai or aadu waari chai; at level 4 also half or full), so those rows wait for the tray (`when`). Wave 6 levels, each adding one thing: 1 = one cup; 2 = two; 3 = three; 4 = three plus half/full. Each cup is one card with a fixed shape (`card`). Tastes are only a bias (tasteChance). Zafar 29 Sept: a cup with no milk, or with milk but no sugar, is sometimes (`named`) ordered by the chai's own name, *Muke kari chai khape.* / *Muke mori chai khape.*, as that person's card headline (`personHead`); its rows still say what the name means (dudh na / khun na).
chai.how: Each person says how they like their chai. Make every cup their way.

card._about: Wave 6: a cup's card always has these slots, in this order (an empty slot when the chai is plain). `optional` slots show only when someone in this order has them. 29 Sept (X1, Zafar): the extra (aadu / elchi) is the TOP row, since the headline names it (Muke aadu waari chai khape.), then milk, then sugar; said in this order too.

maani._about: The Maani line (data/stations/maani-line.json): which kind and how many, in Kutchi. The tally's kinds are said in a random order; the bowls always offer both doughs. Wave 6 levels, each adding one thing: 1 = one maani (which kind: listen); 2 = two, any mix; 3 = three with both kinds, (one tawa at every level: §13's burner rule); 4 = big/small (wadhi/nindhi, she-forms: maani is a she-word), a compound kind ph-big+cook-maani said 'ba wadhi maani'. One card per maani (`cards`).
maani.name: cook-maani
maani._sentence: 29 Sept (X1): the headline names the first kind with its count (Muke ba bajr ji maani khape.); a second kind follows with the join (and, to record)
maani.how: Listen for which maani and how many. Roll each one, then cook it on the tawa.

daal.name: cook-daal

speed._about: S02-B: no speed at level 1 (the stir mechanic asks none there), so the card never shows one it won't ask

say._about: T14 (DAAR-12, S02-B): the stir row on the card: the laps and the speed asked (from level 2), shown when the stir starts

daal._about: Chop: the order names which vegetables go in (dungri, tameto, marcha: several from level 1); Nani says how many of each at the board. Level 1 chops them all in one timed round; levels 2-3 split the round with a switch (the chop mechanic's `phases`). Daar v3 (29 Sept play-test, D1-D11): one combined station, js/cook/stations/daar.js (the swipe chop again, its pieces waiting on the counter, then the tadka and the stir in one pot on the kitchen kit's hob, serve and taste); the chop, tadka and stir mechanics stay in the lab.
daal.how: Chop what they say, add the spices in the order Nani says, then stir.

chaat.name: ph-chaat

say._qty: 29 Sept (T1, X12): a layer that's chopped first says how many (ba bataato), as its chop does
say._when: CHT-07 (decision 53, T15, S02-B): the layer order is said just before the bowl, by him from his card (js/cook/mechanics/assemble.js), not with the order at the start

chaat.how: Build the bowl in the order they say. Leave out what they say no to.

samosa.name: ph-samosa
samosa._blockHeads: SAM-11: the headline is written without the count (Muke samosa khape.); each block's head carries it
samosa._baseFirst: 30 Sept (Zafar): the base filling (chundo or bataato: each block's first kind) is the first row on the card and said first; the rest stay shuffled (js/cook/order.js)

fillings._minFirst: 29 Sept (S18, Zafar): every samosa has its base filling (the first kind: chundo, or bataato for veg) at least one spoon, named as a row; marcha, dhania and the rest are extras. 'Two samosas, three chillies' can't happen

count2._count2: 30 Sept (Zafar: two different samosas in one order): from level 3, half the orders have a second kind, this many of it (0: none). Its own block on the card; its first strip starts empty

base2._base2: the second kind's base is the other base (chundo or bataato) from the first kind's

say._about: SAM-11 (T16, S02-B): one block per kind of samosa, its head the count and dish (ba samosa), its fillings under it, like sekelo's skewers and maani's kinds. On the card only: the order already says it

samosa.how: Fill them with what they say, fold them, then fry them.

mishkaki.name: ph-sekelo
mishkaki._pepper: Sidebar v2 (Zafar, 28 Sept evening): no English in the item pills. Green pepper (ph-pepper) has no Kutchi word yet (Mum 26 Sept, B34), so it's out of the skewers (lists and tastes) until it's recorded; its art stays filed
mishkaki._about: The order says how many skewers of each kind (a tally: "ba lakri gos, hakri lakri boga": lakri, the skewer, is the tally's `unit`, a she-word, so one is hakri), and when there's a mixed one its pieces in order (Pela gos, ne poi …): meat and the three vegetables, never the same piece twice running. Wave 6 (docs/design-language/ux-principles.md): one card per skewer, always four dots (`cards`), a mixed one naming its pieces on its dots (`cardOf`); the grill is two jobs, one at a time (thread every skewer, then "Go to the barbecue" and grill them; the juggle of both at once is the optional level 4); no chips on the grill (they stay in samosa + fry). Levels, each adding one thing: 1 = one skewer (meat or veg: listen); 2 = two; 3 = two or three, one may be mixed; 4 = three or four, up to two mixed, threading and grilling at once.

lists._mixes: The mixed skewers (28 Sept, design system 12): four pieces, as a skewer holds (data.mechanics.thread.pieces), meat and both vegetables, never the same piece twice running. The old generator drew three pieces (meat and two vegetables once green pepper was out), which no four-piece skewer could match

vegKind._about: 29 Sept (K4, Zafar): no bare boga skewers. A vegetable skewer names its vegetable (hakri lakri dungri, like hakri lakri gos: data/stations/mishkaki-grill.json kinds only:<piece>); a mixed one lists its pieces in order

skewers._min: 29 Sept (K4): mostly mixed from level 3 (one of two or three; two of three or four at level 4). 30 Sept (sekelo session): level 3 may have two mixed (one mix, said once: ba lakri mixed), so half or more are mixed on most orders; level 4 stays at two (two different mixes are graded one of each)

pattern2._about: Design system 12 (28 Sept): at level 4 two mixed skewers can be two different mixes, each said as its own list and drawn as its own row ('hakri lakri mixed') with its pieces

mishkaki.how: Thread each skewer the way they say. Then take them to the barbecue.

passme.name: Pass me

pour.name: Pour

watch.name: Boil

count.name: Count in

knead.name: Knead

roll.name: Roll

tadka.name: Tadka

mechanics._about: Difficulty as data. Each mechanic's levels: level 1 is the Phase A game exactly; each later level lists only what changes. `profiles` hold settings for one use of a mechanic (pour into a cup). Upgrades change knobs through upgrades[].knobs. Timings are fractions of a ring (0-1) and rates are ring-fills per second. A combined station's own levels can live in data/stations/<id>.json.

fetch._about: Pantry v3 (29 Sept): positions measured from assets/cook/bg/bg-pantry-v3-1600.webp in the 1600x900 world (the shelves, the fridge's three levels and the long tray laid out from sources/art/pantry-v2/pantry-v3-layout-sketch.png). slots: where an item stands (x centre, y its base, w/h its box before the item's shelf size); zone shelf or fridge. fridge: the items that only ever go in the fridge (everything else goes on the shelves). tray: the row of spaces on the tray (x0/x1 its inside, y the base, w/h an item's box there, gap between spaces; front: the tray's front edge [x, y, w, h] in the picture, drawn again over what's on the tray). tally: the tally's centre in the pantry, on the fridge's steel base, clear of everything. fridgeMin: the smallest size a thing is drawn at in the fridge.

levels._pourMs: Wave 6b: a tap pours one measure (to the next dashed line) in this long; the hold knobs (rate, auto, stickMs, minPour, bandScale, spillScore) are only for Cook.Pour.hold, which Cook no longer uses

assemble._about: Chaat v2 (docs/design-language/ui-design-system.md §14, §14a): level 1 has no decoys; from level 2 decoys stand on the shelf with the order's toppings (and, from level 3, the 'don't' item). flyMs: a spoonful's flight to the glass.

thread._about: The Mishkaki grill's board (js/cook/mechanics/thread.js): pieces per skewer (the mixed pattern is 4 long too), decoy bowls from decoyPool (a piece that fits no skewer), and how long after Nani's spoken hint the piece glows (being shown costs the ear star).

grill._about: The Mishkaki grill (js/cook/mechanics/grill.js): each skewer's ring (band, rate in rings per second, rateSpread so they drift apart), turns before the lift, how many cook at once (spots), rack slots (fixed per level, never the number ordered), burntScore, and ignoreBelow (a tap this early in a ring is ignored: no accidental double taps).

levels._rack: 30 Sept (K9, Q11): the rack is a picture of 0-4 skewers, so 4 at every level (the order is 3-4 at level 4; was 5)

art._about: Painted props to load besides the built-in ones and those named by a word's image (assets/cook/props/<name>.webp), e.g. a new dish's omelette-raw / omelette-done.

sprites._about: Painted item sprites (ChatGPT batch 1, build/reports/chatgpt-batch-1.md), wired over the drawn Phase A art, which stays as the fallback (js/cook/art.js). items: item id (a word id, or a thing: pan, tawa, glass…) -> state -> file stem in `dir` (<stem>.png is the source, <stem>.webp what the game loads; build/sprites_webp.py makes the webp: trimmed, max `max` px, or exactly `w` px wide for a prop it replaces, `square` makes it a circle's box). A word's `bowl` is how it shows on a worktop row (the pantry keeps its props and drawn bowls: its shelves need front views), `whole` flies in the chop, `raw`/`grilled`/`charred` go on a skewer. art: a drawn Art key -> item.state (frames: bake the sprite into the drawing's canvas, at box [x, y, w, h], so every scale and crop in the code still fits). props: a painted prop (assets/cook/props) -> item.state loaded under the prop's name instead. vessels: where a vessel sprite's opening is, as fractions of the sprite [cx, cy, rx, ry] plus the depth of its inside (the liquid and the dashed lines sit in it); size scales it against the drawn one's opening; filled: the sprite already shows what's in it (the kadai's oil), so no liquid is drawn over it. bg: a worktop view -> a 1600x900 webp in assets/cook/bg (day only: the game has no evening or night yet). need: what a station or mechanic loads before it builds (only those; anything else falls back to the drawing and loads for next time). tool-chakla-t and veg-dungri-whole-t now wired (art.chakla; veg-02.whole, the daal chop). Left out on purpose (no station reads that state yet, or a design call): veg-dungri-peeled-t (no peel step, only whole -> chopped), tool-velan-t (the rolling pin is part of the two-hand grip, js/cook/hands.js), vessel-thali-t (vessel:serving already uses chaat-bowl; swapping to a flat thali needs Zafar's call on dishes other than chaat). tools: a painted tool drawn into a drawn hand (Wave 6b).

tools._about: Wave 6b: a painted tool in a drawn hand (js/cook/art.js): a drawn Art key -> item.state. The sprite (drawn corner to corner, tip top-left) is turned upright into the hand's own canvas, so every scale and angle in the code stays the same; the skewer's bamboo stick replaces the drawn one above its wooden handle (js/cook/mechanics/grill.js). The chakla now uses batch 2's redraw (data.art.sprites.art.chakla, js/cook/art.js). Not yet: the velan (the rolling pin is drawn as part of the two-hand grip, js/cook/hands.js).

shelf._about: Pantry v2 (28 Sept, docs/archive/art-prompts/chatgpt-art-prompts-pantry-jars.md): each item as a side-on container for the pantry's shelves and fridge, `<id>.shelf` -> [file stem, size]. size is the container's real height against a tall jar (1), so a spice jar never shows as big as the flour; the fetch mechanic multiplies its slot's box by it. Cut by build/cut_pantry_v2.py; bare (no label) until Zafar decides on labels.

s02._about: S02-B: the art run s02's Cook pictures (build/tools/art/specs/s02.run.yaml), by the id the game asks for. Until a line lands, `ready` is false and the game keeps the current art (or a drawn stand-in). When /art-run cuts one: set `file` (the game's webp), `ready: true` and the measured `meta` (sizes, registration points, the flat inner area). Nothing else changes in code.

meta.trays: three tray spots in design px [x, y, w, h], measured on the cut

meta._about: one webp per dish at the counter's angle, shadow to the right

lookalike_groups._about: Pass me shows three pictures from ONE group, so the answer never stands out as the odd one out (docs/archive/cook/cook-with-nani-kutchi-audit.md). Groups keep photos with photos and drawn bowls with bowls, so the picture style gives nothing away either.

calm._about: Wave 5 (clarity and calm): how much Nani says. quietMs: at the start of every station she says nothing for this long (no hints) so the player can work it out. hintMs: how long you can hesitate before she says the word again, by word stage 1-4 (then it glows a few seconds later). passMeChance: the chance she asks for something at a safe moment (never in the first order of a session; at most once an order at level 1). Wave 6: bulbMs = how long the light bulb shows English, by the order's level (5, 3, 2, 1 s); coachSteps = how many moves the first-time overlay shows at a station before it's gone; uiAfter = after how many orders the stars and the light bulb fade in (a new player's first order has only the order card).
calm._passMeS02: S02-B (T19, MAA-14): passMeAfterPlays = how many orders of a dish before Nani's 'pass me' can come (never in the first plays); passMeRingMs = her ring's time (3 s) once she has asked; the game pauses while she's on screen

timing._about: Cook timers by level (design system §11): flip, boil and fry timers get about 15% quicker per level (a rate is multiplied by (1/(1 - levelSpeed))^(level - 1)). Read by the maani station v2; the other stations adopt it as they are rebuilt.

lab._about: Wave 6b (the quality pass, Q4 and Q9 item 6): the Station lab lists the nine kept stations (lab entry keys, in this order); every other entry (the sub-mechanics: pour, boil, count, roll, flip, thread, grill…) sits under 'Parts' for testing. Knead is cut (its file isn't loaded).
lab._notInLaunch: Decision 62 (DAAR-15, S02-B): Tadka stays in the labs (the Station lab and labs.html) but is not in the first launch: Daar replaced it. A launch build leaves out every station listed here.

onboard._about: Wave 6b (docs/design-language/ux-principles.md 8 and 10): the first-time onboarding script for each kept station, run by the shared kit (js/shared/onboard.js) through js/cook/coach.js. Each step is one move the overlay shows: everything dims except the next thing to do (the station's own 'what to do next', Cook.expect), a ghost hand does `do` once (tap, swipe, stir, roll, hold), the child does it, then the next. After the last step the overlay is gone at that station for good (once per profile). `what` says what the step is, for people reading this. Only the guided first time (a dish's first order; the Station lab with 'Nani helps'). Keys are the stations' own keys (Cook.Stations.begin).

the big knob: the burner lights

thread.what: a bowl: the piece slides down the skewer
the last piece: the skewer is full

grill.what: a skewer on the rack: onto the grill
turn it again on the green
lift it onto the plate on the green

daar.what: slice a vegetable Nani named: its pieces go to the side
and another, before the timer runs out

tadka.what: the first spice she said, into the hot oil
the next one (or the pan: tip it into the pot)

stir.what: drag the ladle round the pot, counting the laps

assemble.what: the first topping they said: the bottom layer

fill.what: a spoon of the first filling they said

fry.what: lift it out on the green

samosa.what: a spoon of the first filling they said, onto the strip
the next spoon (as many as the card says)
the tick when the filling's in
fold the strip over the filling

_phases._about: 29 Sept (X11): every phase of every station, by the key its coach runs under (St.begin or St.coach). build/check_onboard.mjs fails when one has no script above, or when a station's code starts a phase this list doesn't know.

guide._about: 28 Sept (Zafar): Nani's guide box at the top of the sidebar says what to do NOW, in Kutchi. Until 5 Oct none was recorded, so each showed as an English placeholder flagged 'to record' (build/reports/cook-ui-28sept.md lists them). W1, 5 Oct: Mum's Round 4 answers give ten of them a `line` (guide-*: add, watch, knead, flip, stir, chop, fold, fry, fill, chai-tray:knob; build/reports/w1-words.md); the rest stay flagged placeholders (pour, roll, the pantry headline and others Mum hasn't answered). Once Mum records one, give it a `line` (a key in `lines`) and the box shows and says that instead. Keys: a station (data.stations), or station:phase. While Nani says one of her own lines at a station (Hane …!, Bareto!, Jaldi kar!), the box shows that line.
